title: Gold on the Harmandir
hookLine: he covers the Harmandir in gilded copper and marble, and it becomes the Golden Temple

lines: MIST ON THE POOL AT DAWN.
cards: Early morning at Amritsar. Mist on the water, kirtan carrying across the pool, and in the middle of it all a building that catches the first light and throws it back gold.

People photograph that glow from every side of the pool. But the building wasn't always gold. This path has watched it rise, be desecrated, be blown up, and be rebuilt by the misls with plain hands and hard work.
Today, someone covers it in light.

teach.h: DOORS ON EVERY SIDE, OPEN TO ALL.
teach.b: Begin with what it already was: the Harmandir Sahib, also called Darbar Sahib, the court of the Lord. Guru Arjan built it in the middle of the pool at Amritsar and placed the scripture inside.
Tradition loves one detail: doors on every side, open to anyone from any direction.
Then the hard years, when it was attacked and destroyed more than once, and the misls rebuilt it. Now Ranjit Singh. With a kingdom behind him, he gave the Harmandir its gold.
The upper part was covered with copper plates, and the copper was gilded, given a skin of gold. The lower walls were faced with marble, inlaid with stones and flower patterns.
Craftsmen worked on it a long time, and slowly the building Sikhs called the Harmandir became the one the world calls the Golden Temple. Here's what matters. He didn't build a temple of his own.
He took the Gurus' house, built by Guru Arjan and rebuilt by ordinary Sikhs, and gilded it. Once more, the king's wealth pointed past the king.

In the Guru Granth Sahib, a hymn of Guru Arjan says that God himself stood up to finish the work of the saints; tradition links it to the finishing of the pool, and it is still sung when a piece of work is finished.
The gold says the same thing in metal: this work is the Guru's, and the best there is belongs here.

how: Sikhs visit the Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar, walk around the pool, listen to kirtan and serve in the langar; the gilded upper walls date from Maharaja Ranjit Singh's time.

o: the Gurus' house in the pool at Amritsar
the throne facing the shrine across the walkway
a palace Ranjit Singh built for himself

games.q: the house that glows — tap the pairs.
p: built the Harmandir in the pool
rebuilt it after it was destroyed
open to anyone from any direction

s: the Harmandir was golden from the day Guru Arjan built it
the gold came much later, given by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
the gold is gilding over copper
copper plates covered in a skin of gold, with marble on the lower walls.
Ranjit Singh built a new temple of his own beside the pool
he gilded the Gurus' house itself rather than building one of his own.

games.q: you're the Maharaja, rich at last. the Harmandir stands, rebuilt by the misls. what do you do with your wealth?
o: build a grander temple of your own somewhere else.
cover the Gurus' house in gold and marble.
leave it as it is and spend on the army.
games.why: he gilded the Harmandir itself, the house Guru Arjan built and ordinary Sikhs rebuilt, and it became the building the world calls the Golden Temple.

practice: If you can, pick up one small thing near you that you love but have let go dull, a ring, a frame, a cup, and polish it slowly with a cloth or your sleeve, as if it belonged to someone you honor; if there's nothing to hand, polish it in your mind.
Watch the shine come back and notice your hands while they work, with Waheguru on each breath out if you pray.

wordCard.voice: Harmandir, the house Guru Arjan built at Amritsar, given gilded copper above and marble below by Ranjit Singh. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi for Harmandir, the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar.

carryVoice: Your line: gold for the guru. The Gurus' house, not his. Day nine hundred eleven.
